text:
Sam: Quick follow-up from the precision RFC: Im leaning toward keeping the precision decision in the orchestration layer rather than scattering heuristics into the runtime. Pros/cons?
Jess: Strong +1 for centralizing. We need a clear audit trail and per-decision telemetry so we can triage quality regressions fast. :mag:
Kai: Centralization helps when routing by cost/region, but watch cache effects. Switching precision mid-session can trash KV cache and spike latency.
Maya: Suggestion for contract: client may send optional `precision_hint`. Orchestrator returns a compact `precision_decision` blob. Runtime gets a tiny flag set. Example (human-readable):

  user_hint: prefer_fp8
  orchestration_decision: int8_requant
  fallback_policy: gradual->fp16

Sam: Good. Keep runtime dumb: only obey orchestration flags. No autonomous precision downgrades in runtime except emergencies.
Andrew: Enterprise customers will want per-tenant pins or opt-outs. How do we bake that in without exploding policy complexity?
Maya: Treat per-tenant overrides as highest-priority rules in the policy engine. Orchestrator evaluates: tenant override -> route-level policy -> workload hints.
Jess: Telemetry we must emit per decision: decision_id, precision_requested, precision_applied, deg_score, latency_p50/p95, kv_cache_hit_rate. Those let us correlate regressions to decisions.
Kai: For cache issues, add `kv_cache_stability` score to the decision. Orchestrator should avoid switches when stability is low.
Sam: Rollback playbook: if deg_score exceeds X for Y minutes, orchestrator auto-rolls back that precision for impacted routes and files an Ops ticket. Human review required for tenant-scoped rollbacks.
InfraBot: canary results: "precision-orch-canary-2026-05" finished: 8k reqs, avg latency +2.8ms, median deg_score 0.018, 9 error events.
Andrew: Investigating errors now. Are they concentrated on longctx or particular prompt shapes? If so we need prompt-shape guard in the policy.
Maya: Minimal decision payload to runtime (to keep RPC small):

  precision_decision: "int8_requant"
  decision_id: "d-1748889999-01"
  kv_cache_action: "no_invalidate"
  stability_ttl_sec: "600"

Jess: Default stability_ttl: 600s for chat, 30s for ephemeral. Make TTL overridable by tenant rule.
Kai: Runtime change: accept {precision, requant, kv_cache_action, decision_id}. If we see the same decision_id we reuse KV state; if different we follow kv_cache_action.
Sam: Test matrix to run prior to rollout: short vs long prompts x fp8/int8/4bit x kv_cache_stability high/low. Shadow traffic + synthetic tests.
Andrew: Compliance note: keep decision audit (decision_id, trigger, timestamp, policy_version) for Private deployments.
Maya: I'll draft the orchestration->runtime boundary API and the ops runbook today, include sample queries for deg_score baselining.
Jess: Agree. Centralized decisions = single place to evolve policies + easier instrumentation. :+1:
Sam: Action items: update RFC to orchestration-first flow, add small runtime flag contract, add telemetry schema and rollout checklist, include per-tenant override story.
Kai: Also add a canary monitoring rule: if kv_cache_hit_rate drops >20% post-decision, pause rollout.
InfraBot: playbook PR: https://git.internal/redwood/precision-orch-playbook/pull/42
Maya: Pinged @Jess @Kai @Andrew for review. Will post draft link in 20m.
Andrew: Thanks all.
Sam: End thread.
